otherProblems: After Close voting the VOTE NOW badge is removed but its space is kept, so every later state (closed, final result, winner) has a noticeably deeper empty band above the question than the panel's other margins (G-17 to G-19, G-24, G-51).

Long names and the long question fit with no clipping or overlap. otherProblems: G-4/G-5: the Day line reads "DAY DAY 2 ·". A hard-coded "DAY" prefix is stacked on a value that already says Day, and viewers will see the doubled word.

otherProblems: G-6/G-7 (empty values): the panel keeps its full height, but only the question and the '0 VOTES / VOTING OPEN' footer remain, stacked in the top half. The lower half of the navy panel is empty and looks broken.

G-26–G-31: pressing Call the winner straight after the Take does nothing on screen. The winner is only flagged after Show result has been pressed.
answer.reasons: The main design is elegant and readable. All three operator actions are offered and work in order. As delivered, though, the closed and result states have an empty band at the top where the badge used to be. The empty-values state leaves the lower half of the panel bare, and the long-value footer duplicates the vote count and the status in clumsy formatting. None of these is a hard collision or clip, but together a viewer would notice them, and a director would send it back for fixes before air.

otherProblems: G-4/G-5: the graphic puts its own 'DAY' label in front of the day field, so a typed 'Day 2 · Auditorium Åsa' comes out on air as 'DAY DAY 2 · AUDITORIUM ÅSA'. A viewer will read the doubled word as a mistake, and operators retyping the day each morning can easily trigger it.

G-4/G-14: with long values the corner ident grows into a large five- or six-line block, and the logo floats alone, centred against the whole stack. The brief asked for a small, calm ident.

otherProblems: G-4/G-5: the day line reads "DAY DAY 2 ·". The graphic adds its own "DAY" prefix to whatever the operator types, so a natural entry doubles the word on air.

otherProblems: The crest only shows with the long values (G-4/G-5). None of the brief-value frames (G-2, G-3 and the step frames) show a crest, so the card's layout without a crest and with one could not be compared using the brief's own values.

otherProblems: With the long race name (G-4, G-5, G-32 to G-36) the panel gets wider but the title still wraps at a narrower width. answer.reasons: This is a tidy, compact strip in the top-right corner: dark panel, a SET header, both team names with the serve dot, a column for sets and a yellow block for current points. It reads clearly on both the dark and the light background. The long Polish names, with all their accents, fit in every stress frame without clipping. The longer name wraps cleanly onto two lines and the row grows to fit. Point A, Point B and Swap all move the serve dot correctly. The final look swaps the header to an amber 'KONIEC' and keeps only the sets column, which is a clear, designed final state. The Take and Out animations are clean slide-and-fades. End set was only tested at 0–0, where no team is ahead, so the frames don't show it working. Nothing a viewer would notice keeps it off air.
